correctness.rationale: The scalar Ricker upper comparison x_n<=U_n, U_n→r=1-a exponentially for r∈(0,1), yields summable positive predator log-increments at Delta=0 and strict exponential decline at Delta<0. At neutrality, a putative positive predator limit forces prey eventually below r and contradicts predator stationarity; two scalar Ricker comparisons then give x_n→r. The stable prey multiplier 1-r<1 and slowly varying predator imply (x_n-r)/y_n→-1/(b+r); a reciprocal increment tends db/(b+r)^3, giving n y_n→(b+r)^3/(db) and n(r-x_n)→(b+r)^2/(db). Independently verified the linearization and coefficient symbolically. Strict-invasion rate follows by Cesaro and positive fixed point demonstrates sharpness. The numerical checker tests cases, not the infinity proof.
